topics.description: Polynomial-time verification with logarithmic randomness and a constant number of proof-bit queries characterizes NP.
topics.name: PCP theorem

topics.description: A language belongs to NP when membership is witnessed by a polynomial-length string accepted by a polynomial-time checker.
topics.name: NP witness verification

topics.description: Accepting computations become finite constraints, Boolean clauses and graphs while preserving the existence of a witness.
topics.name: Reduction to three-colouring

topics.description: The Schwartz–Zippel bound limits the fraction of points where a nonzero polynomial vanishes.
topics.name: Polynomial distance

topics.description: Interpolation represents a table on a grid by a unique polynomial with a degree bound in each variable.
topics.name: Low-degree extension

topics.description: A polynomial vanishing on a grid admits a decomposition using the coordinate vanishing polynomials and a certificate expressed by two identities.
topics.name: Vanishing certificates

topics.description: Vertex values and edge differences satisfy polynomial equations exactly when they define a proper three-colouring.
topics.name: Colouring constraints

topics.description: Four pairs of points and lines tables supply the answers read by four low-degree tests, two grid tests and a difference check.
topics.name: Proof tables and checks

topics.description: An honest colouring passes every check, while sufficiently small rejection forces four nearby polynomials to describe a proper colouring.
topics.name: Completeness and soundness

topics.description: Corrected certificate queries test vanishing identities at prescribed points and relate failure on the grid to rejection.
topics.name: Zero-on-grid test

topics.description: Random line queries recover a polynomial value at a prescribed point or bound the probability of accepting a wrong value.
topics.name: Local correction over fields

topics.description: Weighted bit queries and tests of encoded line entries recover a homogeneous observation at a prescribed point, allowing rejection.
topics.name: Local correction on bits

topics.description: Small rejection gives one polynomial whose encoding is close to the points table on both full and homogeneous labels.
topics.name: Binary low-degree test

topics.description: A random choice between Hadamard testing and a binary weighted identity tests one encoded line entry for low degree.
topics.name: Inner low-degree test

topics.description: Writing exponents in a fixed number of base digits replaces a line polynomial by a polynomial of fixed total degree.
topics.name: Set-multilinear encoding

topics.description: Agreement with supplied line polynomials at random points yields one nearby polynomial of bounded total degree.
topics.name: Point-versus-line test

topics.description: Weighted interpolation at generator powers tests low degree, with plurality correction turning small rejection into polynomial agreement.
topics.name: Standard low-degree test

topics.description: Agreement between low-degree row and column polynomials produces a nearby bivariate polynomial and consistent values at selected crossings.
topics.name: Bivariate agreement

topics.description: Polynomial labels turn field values and their polynomial expressions into bits and distinguish full, affine and homogeneous observations.
topics.name: Labels and encoding

topics.description: Linearity, unit, product and affine consistency checks test whether a word is close to the encoding of one field value.
topics.name: Hadamard test

topics.description: Linearity testing finds a nearby linear word, and two randomly shifted queries recover a requested value with controlled error.
topics.name: Linearity and self-correction

topics.description: A finite multi-stack machine implements the verifier or witness checker with polynomial running time.
topics.name: Polynomial-time implementation

topics.description: A verifier selects an adaptive query tree from its input and random seed, with explicit acceptance probabilities and proof-address bounds.
topics.name: Verifier and query trees

topics.description: Query counts, fair-bit sampling, proof length and independent repetition give the resource bounds and final soundness error.
topics.name: Queries, randomness and repetition
